definitions.title: Threshold KK cascades, dark matter and irreducible freeze-in
definitions.question: What threshold law controls intra-tower KK-graviton decays, and what does it imply for cascading dark matter and for freeze-in populations even when KK gravitons are not dark matter?
definitions.summary: The 2026 sources report momentum-suppressed threshold rates and challenge earlier fast-cascade estimates. Their amplitude domains and cosmological applications differ; flat-dimension exclusions do not establish exclusion of every warped model.

regimes: Near threshold with comparable daughter masses
assumptions: The broad amplitude claim is bounded by the stated diffeomorphism-invariant two-derivative scalar–gravity setting and treatment of fields and branes.
The irreducible-population constraint uses the stated freeze-in history and reheating bounds.
The earlier s-wave estimate is a rejected comparator in these sources.
conventions: Distinguish daughter momentum from parent mass.
Distinguish a partial decay rate from a summed cascade history.
The freeze-in constraint does not require KK gravitons to constitute dark matter.
excludes: A universal no-go for all gravitational interactions or compactifications
Certification of the announced general proof
Importing the unsupplied companion-paper analysis of warped viability

definitions.readingLimit: Bounded pages from 2609.36234 and 2610.01825v1, the latter dated 1 Oct 2026. Complete derivations, appendices, figures and the companion paper are absent; broad and exclusion claims remain attributed to these sources.

definitions.title: How fast can a KK graviton decay near threshold?
definitions.question: How does an intra-tower KK-graviton decay amplitude and rate scale with daughter momentum near threshold, and which background or coupling assumptions control that scaling?
definitions.summary: A supplied 2026 analysis reports a d-wave rate proportional to the fifth power of daughter momentum near threshold. Its derivation and full domain of generality remain outside the reading performed here.

assumptions: Source-specific gravitational action, couplings and background
Generality beyond the supplied setting remains to be checked
conventions: Compare daughter momentum in the parent rest frame
Distinguish amplitude scaling from phase-space-inclusive rate scaling
excludes: A universal theorem for every geometry, field content or higher-derivative theory
Automatic identity of subsequent cosmological conclusions

definitions.readingLimit: arXiv:2610.01825 supplies abstract/introduction statements and the opening of the decay section, not the proof. arXiv:2609.36234 supplies only a description; agreement of derivations or broad generality cannot be certified.

definitions.title: What flat-dimension bounds survive suppressed KK cascades?
definitions.question: In a flat dark dimension with threshold-suppressed KK-graviton cascades, what observational constraints follow from the irreducibly produced population even if it is not all dark matter?
definitions.summary: A flat-dimension analysis argues that unavoidable production and visible decays constrain reheating and radius even when KK gravitons do not constitute all dark matter. Its numerical exclusion remains an attributed result.

systems: KK gravitons in a flat dark dimension
Standard Model brane and visible decay products
regimes: A subdominant KK population is allowed
assumptions: Flat dark dimension
Reported threshold suppression
Specified brane coupling and thermal history
Applicable BBN and CMB reheating floors
conventions: arXiv:2610.01825 uses m_KK=1/R and the four-dimensional reduced Planck mass
Earlier visible-decay constraints use their own mass histories and coupling parameters
excludes: All warped or multidimensional models
An independently checked numerical exclusion curve
Automatic replacement of every earlier conditional phenomenological calculation

definitions.readingLimit: The source reports exclusion of flat radii approximately R≥0.2 micrometres under its assumptions. The calculation, exclusion figure and adopted reheating bounds are outside the supplied window. Comparison sources do not establish that exclusion independently.

definitions.title: Linear cosmology of decay-induced dark-matter kicks
definitions.question: How do repeated KK-graviton decays affect linear cosmological perturbations, and what do CMB, BAO and weak-lensing data constrain about their kick velocity?
definitions.summary: The analysis constrains a velocity combination in a simplified tower model. Its interpretation as Dark Dimension parameter bounds depends on the assumed decay and mass-evolution laws.

assumptions: Approximately equal daughter masses
Last-decay kicks approximate the relevant velocity history
The historical cascade evolution fixes the modeled time dependence
conventions: The principal data constraint is on a velocity combination, not independent measurements of every tower parameter.
includes: Planck CMB, BAO and KiDS-1000 cosmic-shear analysis
excludes: A nonlinear resolution of the σ8 tension
A demonstrated resolution of the Hubble tension
An updated fit using the later threshold law

definitions.readingLimit: The supplied version is 2311.05318v1, dated 9 Nov 2023. Its abstract reports a bound, while the supplied body states the approximations. The likelihood, nonlinear evolution and consequences of replacing the cascade law were not checked.

definitions.title: What do repeated KK decays do to linear structure?
definitions.question: Within the specified repeated-decay KK-graviton model, how do daughter recoil and the changing mass distribution affect linear cosmological perturbations?
definitions.summary: Repeated decays change the tower mass distribution and give daughters recoil velocities. The linear cosmology calculation assumes a specified decay history and does not establish the cascade microphysics.

targets: Recoil constraints and their conditional parameter interpretation
regimes: Source-era CMB, BAO and cosmic-shear analysis
assumptions: Repeated intra-tower decay evolution
Simplified daughter distribution dominated by approximately symmetric decays
Small released mass difference
conventions: The source's kick parameter is a combination of model parameters
Its reported confidence limit is a dated author result
excludes: Nonlinear structure predictions or a demonstrated resolution of the S8 tension
Unconditional viability of the cascade
Visible-energy injection as the primary target

definitions.readingLimit: The model assumptions and abstract's reported kick constraint were read. Perturbation equations, likelihood implementation and numerical constraints were not independently checked.

definitions.title: Modulus and gravitino cosmology
definitions.question: When do modulus or gravitino production, domination and decay permit BBN-compatible histories and acceptable dark-matter abundances?
definitions.summary: Connects decay timing, production, annihilation and dilution while preserving stable-gravitino, thermal-WIMP and nonthermal-neutralino alternatives.

systems: Cosmological moduli and other specified heavy scalars
regimes: Stable gravitinos as a separate alternative
assumptions: Dominance, branching fractions and mass ordering are model-specific
conventions: Successful BBN timing does not by itself certify gravitino, LSP or axion safety
includes: G2-MSSM, LVS and effective decay cosmologies
Superheavy dark matter diluted by a lighter modulus
excludes: Treating every modulus as the producer of the surviving dark matter

definitions.readingLimit: The excerpts establish announced targets and selected mechanisms, not complete parameter-space validation.

definitions.title: How do early matter domination and dilution change relic abundance?
definitions.question: How do production timing and entropy release in specified early matter- or modulus-dominated histories determine dark-matter abundance and allowed duration, subject to the relevant reheating, inflationary and dark-radiation constraints?
definitions.summary: Production and dilution can impose competing constraints on an early matter-dominated history. Superheavy neutralinos provide a two-stage example; different relics retain their own channels and expansion histories.

systems: Dark-matter relics and a dominant matter-like field or modulus
targets: Allowed duration of early matter domination
Competition between dilution requirements and inflationary bounds
regimes: Source-specific early matter or modulus domination
Production before domination, during its adiabatic stage or through decay, as specified separately
assumptions: A specified expansion and reheating history
Production channels, branching fractions and sector temperatures remain model-specific
conventions: arXiv:1808.02659's comparison cross section is 3×10^−26 cm^3 s^−1
The EDGES interpretation in arXiv:1812.11915 remains a paper-specific premise
A sufficiently long dilution phase is not by itself a sufficient condition for full viability
includes: BBN reheating floors as boundary inputs
excludes: Scalar-tensor expansion changes automatically identified with entropy dilution
A universal relic formula or duration bound
Current validation of historical anomaly interpretations

definitions.readingLimit: Only arXiv:2010.03573 supplies excerpts for this card. They support the two-stage history, branching-condition statement and opposing duration constraints, but not the complete numerical solution or model scan. Other contributions are description-level.

definitions.title: Observable Standard Model decays of KK-graviton dark matter
definitions.question: What bounds do cosmological energy deposition and photon or positron signals place on KK-graviton dark matter and its coupling to the Standard Model brane?
definitions.summary: The supplied analysis constrains decay signals and a phenomenological brane-overlap coupling within its tower-evolution model. Naturalness-based mass conclusions require the additional coupling assumption.

assumptions: The 2023 tower mass history and cascade prescription are conditional historical inputs.
The natural-mass interpretation assumes order-one dimensionless decay couplings.
conventions: λ denotes averaged graviton wave-function overlap with the brane.
includes: CMB, IGM heating, diffuse and Galactic photons, and Galactic positrons
excludes: An unconditional present-day dark-matter mass bound
Treating the assumed cascade history as established after the supplied 2026 critiques

definitions.readingLimit: Bounded pages from 2307.11048 support the targets and reported conditional bounds. One source-object evidence item is omitted. The 2026 excerpts challenge the cascade premise; they do not supply a complete reanalysis of these observables.

definitions.title: How does a hot brane produce KK gravitons?
definitions.question: Can a hot Standard Model brane gravitationally produce the KK-graviton abundance needed in the Dark Dimension setting, for specified initial brane temperature and bulk population?
definitions.summary: A hot Standard Model brane can populate a KK-graviton tower in the specified scenario. The initial abundance question is separate from whether the population survives as dark matter.

systems: Standard Model brane and KK-graviton tower
regimes: Early-universe hot-brane production in the specified Dark Dimension setup
assumptions: Specified initial brane temperature
Bulk initially essentially unexcited in the arXiv:2311.05318 setup
Gravitational brane coupling
conventions: An initially adequate abundance does not establish viable late-time dark matter
excludes: All gravitational or nonthermal dark-matter production
Independent validation of a fast subsequent cascade
UHECR spectral measurements

definitions.readingLimit: No production integral or abundance calculation was checked. The source excerpts state inherited production assumptions and claimed abundances; the late-time cascade is disputed elsewhere in this packet.
